source_lines.51: 2.1 Explicit contraction of every augmented row. For $r\geq0$ let $\mathrm{ins}_r:S^r\to S^{r+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate, with $S^0=\mathrm{pt}$; so $\mathrm{ins}_0$ is the point $y$ itself. The deletion and insertion maps satisfy $d_0\,\mathrm{ins}_{r+1}=\mathrm{id}$ and $d_i\,\mathrm{ins}_{r+1}=\mathrm{ins}_r\,d_{i-1}$ for $i>0$. Put $h_{p+1}:=\mathrm{ins}_{p+1}^*:H^q(S^{p+2},K)\to H^q(S^{p+1},K)$ and $h_0:=\mathrm{ins}_0^*:H^q(S,K)\to H^q(K)$, with $\delta_{-1}$ the constant pullback of the projection $S\to\mathrm{pt}$. Applying the two identities termwise gives $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\mathrm{id}$ for every $p\geq0$: the $i=0$ term of $h_{p+1}\delta_p$ is the identity, and the terms $i>0$ are the negatives of $\delta_{p-1}h_p$; moreover $h_0\delta_{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, because the projection followed by the chosen point is the identity of $\mathrm{pt}$. Hence every augmented horizontal row is contractible, in particular exact, in every internal degree $q$, using only functorial pullback on cohomology. [step 1.2, algebra]

source_lines.30: For a bicosimplicial complex $K^{p,r,q}$ of modules over a commutative ring, with $p,r\geq0$ and one fixed lower bound $q\geq a$, the alternating-face total complex and the diagonal alternating-face total complex are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent:
source_lines.32: On the left total degree is $p+r+q$ and differential is $\delta_h+(-1)^p\delta_v+(-1)^{p+r}d$; on the right total degree is $n+q$ and differential is $\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}+(-1)^nd$. These comparisons preserve augmentation and apply to coherent derived diagrams after a supplied functorial strict resolution. They require no dimensional finiteness of the coefficient modules and no choice principle. Normalization can be applied on either side without changing the conclusion.
source_lines.36: **Given:** $K^{p,r,q}=0$ unless $p,r\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. Horizontal cofaces $d_h^i:K^{p,r,q}\to K^{p+1,r,q}$ and codegeneracies $s_h^i:K^{p,r,q}\to K^{p-1,r,q}$, and the analogous vertical operators, satisfy the cosimplicial identities and commute between directions. The internal differential raises $q$ by one, squares to zero and commutes with these operators. The three $\delta$'s are the corresponding alternating coface sums. The auxiliary bisimplicial modules in steps 1.1–4.1 instead have faces lowering degree and degeneracies raising it; step 5.1 reverses their universal operator formulas.
source_lines.50: 1.1 Universal models and contractions. For a bisimplicial $R$-module $M$, let $Q_{p,r}$ have value $R[\Delta([u],[p])\times\Delta([v],[r])]$ at $(u,v)$. An element $x\in M_{p,r}$ determines the unique map $Q_{p,r}\to M$ sending the universal generator to $x$. The diagonal chain complex of $Q_{p,r}$ consists of pairs of monotone vertex strings; define $h$ on each basis string by prepending $(0,0)$. Deleting the first vertex gives the original string, and every other deletion commutes with prepending with its index reduced by one. Thus $\partial h+h\partial=1-e$, where $e$ sends every degree-zero vertex to $(0,0)$ and is zero in positive degrees. On the double total, identified with $C_*(\Delta[p];R)\otimes_R C_*(\Delta[r];R)$, use the separate prepend-zero contractions $h_p,h_r$ and projectors $e_p,e_r$. For homogeneous $x$, set $H(x\otimes y)=h_p(x)\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}e_p(x)\otimes h_r(y)$. The Koszul differential gives $\partial H+H\partial=(1-e_p)\otimes1+e_p\otimes(1-e_r)=1-e_p\otimes e_r$. These contractions fill every positive-degree cycle and every augmentation-zero degree-zero cycle by specified finite chains. Unlike a constant simplicial map on unnormalized chains, $e$ is supported only in degree zero. [F3, F4, construct, algebra]
source_lines.52: 2.1 Diagonal-to-total comparison. Put $\operatorname{Diag}_m(M)=M_{m,m}$ and $\operatorname{Tot}_m(M)=\bigoplus_{p+r=m}M_{p,r}$ with the Koszul boundary. Set $\varphi_0=1$. Inductively evaluate $\varphi_{m-1}\partial z$ on the universal generator $z$ of $Q_{m,m}$, and fill it using the total contraction of step 1.1. It is a cycle because $\partial\varphi_{m-1}=\varphi_{m-2}\partial$; when $m=1$, it is the difference of the two endpoint vertices and has augmentation zero. Evaluate that specified filling under the representing map for each $x\in M_{m,m}$ to define $\varphi_m(x)$. This is linear and natural, and its boundary is $\varphi_{m-1}\partial x$. Thus $\varphi$ is a natural chain map, given degreewise by finite linear combinations of structure operators. [step 1.1, construct]
source_lines.54: 3.1 Total-to-diagonal comparison. Set $\psi_0=1$. For each summand $M_{p,r}$ in total degree $m=p+r>0$, evaluate $\psi_{m-1}\partial z$ on the universal generator of $Q_{p,r}$ and fill it with the diagonal contraction of step 1.1. The induction hypothesis makes it a cycle; in degree $m=1$ its two endpoint coefficients cancel. Evaluate the filling under the representing map of each element of $M_{p,r}$ and sum over $p+r=m$. This defines a linear natural chain map $\psi$, again by specified finite operator formulas. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]
source_lines.56: 4.1 Homotopy inverses. Let $C,C'$ each be the diagonal or total chain functor, and let $f,g:C\to C'$ be natural chain maps with $f_0=g_0$. Set $h_0=0$. For $m\geq1$, on a universal generator $z$ of a representing summand of $C_m$, put $\beta_m=(f_m-g_m)(z)-h_{m-1}(\partial z)$. The previously established equation $\partial h_{m-1}+h_{m-2}\partial=f_{m-1}-g_{m-1}$ makes $\partial\beta_m=0$. This cycle has positive degree, so its specified model contraction gives $h_m(z)$ with $\partial h_m(z)=\beta_m$. Extend by representing maps. Then $\partial h+h\partial=f-g$. Apply this to $\psi\varphi$ and $1$ on the diagonal, and to $\varphi\psi$ and $1$ on the total; both composites are the identity in degree zero. The resulting natural homotopies have finite operator formulas. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]
source_lines.58: 5.1 Cosimplicial variance and the internal differential. The maps and homotopies of steps 2.1–4.1 are finite linear combinations of morphisms in the simplex categories. Their identities can be tested on the free representables of step 1.1, so they are universal additive operator identities. Reverse every operator and every composition to obtain cochain maps in the opposite directions and cochain homotopies lowering simplicial total degree by one. This reverses the two homotopy-inverse identities, without taking algebraic duals. Apply these formulas in each internal degree $q$. Naturality makes them commute with $d$. A comparison preserves simplicial total degree $t=p+r=n$, so it commutes with the signed internal differential $(-1)^td$. For a homotopy $H$ lowering $t$ by one, the internal terms in $DH+HD$ are $(-1)^{t-1}dH+(-1)^tHd=0$. Hence the comparisons and homotopies apply to precisely the two cochain differentials in the Statement. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

source_lines.126: 1.1 The orbit map $G\to N$, $g\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}(g)e$, has irreducible image closure. By [F1] its image has dimension $\dim\mathfrak g-\dim Z_{\mathfrak g}(e)=2|\Phi^+|=\dim N$; by [F6] the constructible image is dense and therefore contains a nonempty open subset of the irreducible variety $N$. The orbit is $G$-stable, so its translates of this open subset cover the orbit; consequently $G\cdot e$ is open in $N$. [F1, F6, algebra]
source_lines.128: 1.2 The Springer map is $$\mu:G\times^B\mathfrak n^+\longrightarrow N,\qquad[g,x]\longmapsto\operatorname{Ad}(g)x.$$ Its graph is the incidence subvariety $$\{(gB,y)\in X\times N:y\in\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+\},$$ which is closed because the spaces $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+$ form a vector subbundle of $X\times\mathfrak g$. The projection $X\times N\to N$ is projective by [F4], so $\mu$ is proper by the projective-morphism theorem included in [F4]. Surjectivity follows from the last clause of [F1]. [F1, F4]
source_lines.132: 3.1 The fiber over $e$ is a single point. Indeed, if $e\in\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+$, write $g=b_1n_wb_2$ by [F3]. The element $x=\operatorname{Ad}(b_1^{-1})e$ still has every simple coefficient nonzero by [F2]. Since $\operatorname{Ad}(n_w^{-1})x\in\mathfrak n^+$, each nonzero simple-root component of $x$ must map to a positive root space; distinct root spaces cannot cancel. Therefore $w^{-1}$ sends every positive simple root to a positive root, so $w=1$ by [F3], and $gB=B$. This algebraic argument holds after every algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb C$ as well. Equivariance gives a singleton geometric fiber over every point of $O=G\cdot e$. The restriction $\mu_O:\mu^{-1}(O)\to O$ is proper by base change. Its fibers are finite type and their geometric point sets are singletons, so each fiber point is isolated and has residue field finite over the base residue field; the finite-fiber criterion in [F8] makes $\mu_O$ quasi-finite, and proper quasi-finite finiteness in [F8] makes it finite. Both source and target are integral of dimension $2|\Phi^+|$, so the induced function-field extension is finite. It is separable in characteristic zero, and by [F9] has a primitive element $\theta$. After replacing an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq O$ by a smaller nonempty principal open, its finite preimage is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite over $A$, $\theta$ lies in $B$, and $B=A[\theta]\cong A[T]/(f)$ for the monic minimal polynomial $f$ of $\theta$: first clear denominators to place $\theta$ in $B$, then localize to kill the finite torsion quotient $B/A[\theta]$ and to put the coefficients of $f$ in $A$. The discriminant of $f$ is nonzero by separability, so after inverting it this finite map is étale of rank $d=[\operatorname{Frac}B:\operatorname{Frac}A]$. Every geometric closed fiber in this open then has $d$ distinct points, but every geometric fiber over $O$ is a singleton; therefore $d=1$. This proves birationality without inferring degree from a closed-point count alone. [F2, F3, F8, F9, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2]

source_lines.59: In $S_4$, written in one-line notation, let $b:=s_2=1324$ and $w:=s_2s_1s_3s_2=3412$ (a reduced word of length $4$; the two middle generators commute). (a) The interval $[b,w]$ has exactly ten elements: $1324$; $1342,1423,2314,3124$; $1432,2413,3142,3214$; and $3412$. (b) For comparable pairs in this interval the only Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial different from $1$ is $P_{b,w}(q)=1+q$; so $\mu(b,w)=1$, and $(b,w)$ is a $\mu$-pair with $\ell(w)-\ell(b)=3>1$: $\mu$-pairs need not be covers. All other $\mu$-pairs inside the interval are covers, and all $r_{y,z}$ for $y,z\in[b,w]$ are the corresponding Laurent polynomials read off from [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. (c) The descent recursion of [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomial-recursion]] at $y=b$, $w$ and $s=s_2$ (a left descent of $w$, with $sw=2413$ and $sb=1234=\mathrm{id}$, so $c=1$) reads $$P_{b,w}(q)=P_{\mathrm{id},2413}(q)+qP_{b,2413}(q)-\!\!\!\sum_{\substack{b\le z\le 2413\\ s_2z<z,\ \mu(z,2413)\ne0}}\!\!\!\mu(z,2413)\,q^{(4-\ell(z))/2}P_{b,z}(q);$$ the sum is empty because $[b,2413]=\{1324,1423,2314,2413\}$ and its only element with $s_2z<z$ is $1324$, for which $\mu(1324,2413)=0$; since $P_{\mathrm{id},2413}=P_{b,2413}=1$, the recursion returns $P_{b,w}=1+q$, in agreement with (b). (d) The inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] is $q'_{b,w}=-v-v^3$, while $q'_{b,1342}=q'_{b,1423}=q'_{b,2314}=q'_{b,3124}=-v$ and $q'_{b,1432}=q'_{b,2413}=q'_{b,3142}=q'_{b,3214}=v^2$; the matrix identity $\sum_zq'_{x,z}p_{z,w}=\delta_{x,w}$ of [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-inversion-formula]] holds on the ten-point interval. In particular the inverse coefficients are not all nonnegative even though all $p_{y,z}$ are.
source_lines.63: 1.1 **The full interval.** The displayed word for $w$ has inversion length $4$, so it is reduced. Its reduced subwords of lengths $0,1,2,3,4$ give respectively $1234$; $1324,2134,1243$; $1342,1423,2314,3124,2143$; $1432,2413,3142,3214$; and $3412$. The four excluded elements $1234,2134,1243,2143$ have no reduced subword $s_2$, so they are not above $b$; the other ten are. For an explicit order check, write $a=1342=s_2s_3$, $c=1423=s_3s_2$, $d=2314=s_1s_2$, $f=3124=s_2s_1$, and $A=1432=s_2s_3s_2$, $C=2413=s_1s_3s_2$, $D=3142=s_2s_1s_3$, $F=3214=s_2s_1s_2$. The reduced-subword criterion gives the intermediate covers $a<A,D$; $c<A,C$; $d<C,F$; $f<D,F$; each rank-two element is also above $b=s_2$, and each rank-three element is below $w$. These are all cover incidences between adjacent ranks, so all other comparisons are their transitive consequences. [F1, algebra]

source_lines.55: 2.1 **Polynomials and covers.** Reading the expansions in step 1.3 gives $p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}$ for every $y\le w$, so [F4] gives $P_{y,w}=1$ and $\mu(y,w)=[v]p_{y,w}$ is $1$ exactly at length difference one. By the reduced-subword criterion [F6], the Bruhat ranks in $S_3$ are $\{123\}$, $\{132,213\}$, $\{231,312\}$, and $\{321\}$, and each element in one of these layers is below every element in the next layer. Hence the covers are precisely the two edges from $123$, the four edges from rank one to rank two, and the two edges into $321$; these are exactly the eight pairs listed. Grading rules out other covers. [F4, F6, step 1.3, algebra]

source_lines.63: 2.1 All degrees and the cyclotomic quotient. By the minimal-polynomial clause of [F1], the operator $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ has minimal polynomial $\prod_j(x-a_j)=x(x+1)$ for every $d\ge1$, so the tensor action factors through $H_d(\mathbf a)$ with $\mathbf a=(0,-1)$, i.e. through $H_d(\Lambda)$ for $\Lambda=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_{-1}$; and by [F2] that quotient has dimension $2^dd!$. At $d=1$ the quotient is $\mathbb C[x]/(x(x+1))\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$, acting on $V$ through $x_1$ as the two-dimensional algebra of operators that are scalar on each of the two eigenspaces of step 1.1; hence the image is semisimple and $V$ is the direct sum of those two eigenspaces. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

On a product chart, [F2] gives the canonical differential-module isomorphism $M=\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes N$, with $N=p_{\alpha*}(\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M)$ in that chart's partial TDO convention. The inverse image in [F1] has relative structure-sheaf factor, so this is precisely the displayed form $\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N$. The proof of [F2] makes its evaluation natural in all commuting base operators; on overlaps it is intertwined by the chain rule and the partial TDO cocycle in [F1]. Thus the base actions glue on the stated direct image and the local isomorphisms glue to the asserted global one. Coherence of $N$ is part of [F2], not an inference from $\mathcal O_X$-coherence of $M$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]
source_lines.79: 3.1 Conversely, the displayed form has local relative factor $\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes N$ by [F1], whose direct image is zero by [F2]; hence $p_{\alpha*}M=0$ globally. Tensoring this form by $\mathcal O_X(-\rho)$ and applying $p_{\alpha*}$ recovers $N$, since $p_{\alpha*}p_\alpha^\dagger N=N$. The same identity proves uniqueness up to the recovered canonical isomorphism. This proves both directions and all higher-image assertions; no rank-one classification is left as a source-only premise. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
